answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, and the primary contract expiring in 14 days with no auto-renew, switching vendors (c2) or adding a second source (c3) both introduce onboarding/integration risk that the plant cannot absorb right now. Deferral (c5) is not viable because this is the critical primary contract, not a non-critical renewal, and finance has mandated an 18% cut this year. Renegotiating with the incumbent (c4) offers a path to real cost reduction (aligning with the 18% mandate) while preserving the stable integration and delivery continuity seen historically with this vendor (c1, c6). I want to verify c4's archived record before committing, since it is a single consolidated memory and the decision hinges on whether the recovered margin was material and whether service scope held, given this is the one sourcing move I can make this cycle. This is applied at full scale (the whole primary contract) because there's no time or capacity buffer for a phased test. I flag downstream risk because single-source concentration remains unaddressed this cycle, and if negotiation fails to land before day 14, we could be forced into a rushed switch under worse conditions.
